questions: How many bars did you pattern and measure for the diode effect, on how many chips and in how many cooldowns, and how many showed the zero-field diode and its reversal? Your Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 4 show two.
Why were any others set aside?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: η versus temperature up to the 350 mK transition, preparation fields beyond ±1 T along [100], and η in small applied fields around zero?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like, for example the [100] bar's ZFC switching-current distributions next to the Fig. 3a inset?
What was the residual field at "H = 0" after a ±1 T or ±4 T excursion, and how did you measure or null it?
If you prepare a state, warm the sample above the Al transition (and far below the 480 K Néel temperature), and cool again at zero field, does η keep its sign?
Were the [010] and [100] bars measured on the same chip and in the same mounting relative to the magnet axes, and could you rotate the chip by 90° so that the crystal axes and the coil axes swap?

Did you run the same protocol on a control film (plain Al, or Al on a nonmagnetic layer), and could you measure R_even on the superconducting heterostructure itself, since Fig. 4 uses a bar from a different wafer at 5 K? In the text I read, refs. 28 to 30 appear in the reference list with no citation in the text; was a discussion of them planned?
